parsed.rationale: The rhythm is regular sinus with very high precordial voltages (deep S in V2–V3 plus tall R in V4–V5, well over 35 mm). The ST elevation in V2–V4 is mild, concave and proportionate to the deep S waves, which fits an LVH repolarization pattern rather than a STEMI. There are no reciprocal changes or convex ST elevation. This tracing therefore doesn't show STEMI criteria, even though your case was an acute STEMI in the end.
